# Requirement for third parties to declare election expenses

**Published: 27th June 2022**

The Jersey Electoral Authority would like to remind any third parties who incurred expenses or received donations relating to the 22 June election that, in certain circumstances, they need to file a declaration with the JEA by 20 July 2022.

Details of what needs to be declared can be found on the [relevant form](https://eur02.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fvotejersey.wpengine.com%2Fwp-content%2Fuploads%2F2022%2F06%2FExpenses-Form-Declaration-by-Third-Party-expenses.doc&data=05%7C01%7C%7C25ea28ab47324dd8a60008da58504488%7C2b5615117ddf495c8164f56ae776c54a%7C0%7C0%7C637919399013093337%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C3000%7C%7C%7C&sdata=hBnng2Lkpl0XT9ZiFuEPzvTEfcdiaz%2FyewgFIRmejJw%3D&reserved=0).

If a declaration is required, it is an offence to fail to deliver one on time without reasonable excuse.

Expenses can be incurred in both campaigning for or against the election of candidates (or political parties). For the avoidance of doubt this would include expenditure encouraging the casting of votes for “None of the candidates”.
